title: Ops Workbench: unified admin utility, scheduled runbooks-as-tasks, and automated responders
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Build a unified Ops Workbench that bundles admin utilities (CLI + lightweight web UI), converts canonical runbooks into task sequences that can be scheduled (cronified) or triggered by alerts, and supports automated responder routines for common support flows. Goal: reduce manual toil for on-call and support engineers, and make runbooks repeatable, auditable, and schedulable.

Scope: admin utilities library (idempotent ops commands), runbook-to-task compiler, scheduling engine, webhook triggers (PagerDuty, GitHub Actions, alertmanager), RBAC for who can run/schedule playbooks, and audit log integration with KMS-backed signing for compliance evidence.
acceptance_criteria: CLI implements 6 core admin commands (token revoke, user-deprovision, cache-warm, model-rollover-safety-check, snapshot-export, emergency-mode-toggle) with idempotent flags and dry-run output
Web UI allows creating a task sequence from a runbook template and scheduling it (cron or one-off) with preview and audit comment
Tasks show progress logs and attach to an incident or support ticket (GitHub Issue or Zendesk) and persist full audit trail
Automation triggers can be bound to a PagerDuty escalation policy or Prometheus alert and can run with scoped ephemeral creds
Playbooks can be parameterized with typed inputs and have guardrails (SLA impact checks) that block destructive steps unless acknowledged by two approvers
End-to-end tests (integration) in CI validate scheduling, RBAC checks, and audit log entries for three representative playbooks

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Accidental destructive runs by misconfigured schedules. Mitigation: two-approver destructive step ack + schedule dry-run preview + operator-level RBAC
Risk: Secrets exposure in scheduled tasks. Mitigation: ephemeral execution creds and recording only references in audit logs (no plaintext secrets), KMS-backed signing
Risk: Scheduler overload from many cron jobs. Mitigation: quota per org/team and burst throttling with backoff and alerting
Risk: Compliance concerns for customer-facing private installs. Mitigation: provide opt-out audit verbosity and local audit collector for Private deployments
testing_plan: Unit tests for CLI commands and compiler transformations
Contract tests for webhook payloads (PagerDuty, Alertmanager, GitHub)
Integration test job in CI that runs a scheduled task against a staging cluster and verifies audit entries
Chaos test: simulate a node loss during a scheduled run and validate graceful retry and no double-execution
deployment_and_rollout: Phase 1: internal-only feature flag; run two canary playbooks for eng/sre teams for 2 weeks
Phase 2: expand to support org + on-call rotation; add billing cost telemetry
Phase 3: GA release with admin console, RBAC, and complete audit-signing support
